reconcile.note: John Gill harmonizes Amasa's father by reading Ithra the Israelite and Jether the Ishmaelite as the same man, dual-named as an ethnic sojourner or proselyte.

discrepancy.emptyNote: Steve Wells's Skeptic's Annotated Bible catalogs the discrepancy plainly, naming Amasa's father Ithra the Israelite in Samuel and Jether the Ishmaelite in Chronicles.
discrepancy.emptyNoteAttr: Steve Wells (2013), The Skeptic's Annotated Bible.

sides.snippet: Amasa was the son of a man, whose name was Ithra the Israelite, who went in to Abigail the daughter of Nahash, sister to Zeruiah, Joab's mother.
sides.verseText: Absalom set Amasa over the host instead of Joab. Now Amasa was the son of a man, whose name was Ithra the Israelite, who went in to Abigail the daughter of Nahash, sister to Zeruiah, Joab's mother.

sides.snippet: Abigail bore Amasa; and the father of Amasa was Jether the Ishmaelite.
sides.verseText: Abigail bore Amasa; and the father of Amasa was Jether the Ishmaelite.
